title: What American C.E.O.s Are Worried About

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《Dealbook》的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的Dealbook峰会上，现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》App进行观看，并免费阅读我们所有的报道一个月。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: For five decades, American corporations have prized profits for shareholders above all else.
sentences.zh: 五十年来，美国企业一直将股东利益放在首位。

sentences.en: Now,
sentences.zh: 如今，

sentences.en: America's most powerful chief executives say it's time to do things differently.
sentences.zh: 美国最具权势的首席执行官们表示，是时候做出改变了。

sentences.en: Andrew Ross-Sorkin on What's Driving That Change.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·罗斯-索金谈推动这一变革的动力。

sentences.en: Wednesday, August 21St. Andrew, tell me what happened in your world on Monday morning.
sentences.zh: 8月21日，星期三。安德鲁，告诉我周一早上你的世界里发生了什么。

sentences.en: On Monday morning, 5 a.m.
sentences.zh: 周一早上，凌晨5点。

sentences.en: in the morning, the Business Roundtable, which is probably the most powerful and influential lobbying organization for the nation's biggest
sentences.zh: 商业圆桌会议——这可能是美国最大企业中权力最大、最具影响力的游说组织，

sentences.en: companies, think Apple, think Amazon, Walmart, J.P.
sentences.zh: 想想苹果、亚马逊、沃尔玛、摩根

sentences.en: Morgan, all of them, came out and said that shareholders were going to be just one piece of a larger puzzle.
sentences.zh: 大通，所有这些公司——发表声明称，股东将只是更大拼图中的一部分。

sentences.en: From the Business Roundtable,
sentences.zh: 代表商业圆桌会议，

sentences.en: 181 of the top CEOs in the country have agreed now that maximizing profits in all situations cannot necessarily be the main goal of corporations.
sentences.zh: 全国181位顶尖CEO现在一致认为，在所有情况下最大化利润不一定能成为企业的主要目标。

sentences.en: Statements signed by almost 200 CEOs, including
sentences.zh: 这份由近200位CEO签署的声明，包括

sentences.en: J.P.
sentences.zh: 摩根

sentences.en: Morgan's Jamie Dimon, says companies should focus on all stakeholders.
sentences.zh: 大通的杰米·戴蒙，称企业应当关注所有利益相关者。

sentences.en: For as long as I covered the world of business, every CEO in America said they had a fiduciary duty to shareholders.
sentences.zh: 在我报道商业世界的这么长时间里，美国的所有CEO都说他们对股东负有信托责任。

sentences.en: Everything was in the name of profits.
sentences.zh: 一切都是以利润的名义。

sentences.en: So after decades of explicitly saying that shareholders were the highest end of a corporation, they point out the corporation's duties to their customers,
sentences.zh: 因此，在明确表示股东是企业最高利益数十年后，他们指出了企业对客户、

sentences.en: to their suppliers, to their communities, and then they get to their shareholders.
sentences.zh: 供应商、社区的责任，最后才轮到股东。

sentences.en: A massive change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的改变。

sentences.en: And so the idea that any of these other stakeholders are even being acknowledged as part of the equation is a major shift.
sentences.zh: 因此，任何其他利益相关者甚至被承认作为方程式的一部分，都是一个重大的转变。

sentences.en: But in many ways, it's a return to an earlier era, an era almost a century ago when these other stakeholders mattered in a way that they haven't for so many years.
sentences.zh: 但在许多方面，这是对早期时代的回归，一个近一个世纪前的时代，当时这些其他利益相关者的重要性在多年来从未有过。

sentences.en: And what is that era?
sentences.zh: 那个时代是什么样的？

sentences.en: If you go back to the 1930s, possibly even earlier, the biggest corporations in America genuinely thought about the full plethora of constituents.
sentences.zh: 如果你回到20世纪30年代，甚至更早，美国最大的企业确实考虑了所有的利益相关群体。

sentences.en: Employees mattered.
sentences.zh: 员工很重要。

sentences.en: Customers mattered.
sentences.zh: 客户很重要。

sentences.en: Suppliers mattered.
sentences.zh: 供应商很重要。

sentences.en: The profits mattered.
sentences.zh: 利润也很重要。

sentences.en: But there was clearly a larger social compact that had been reached between companies and the rest of society.
sentences.zh: 但很显然，企业与社会其他部分之间达成了一种更大的社会契约。

sentences.en: And what did that look like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么样子的？

sentences.en: And what's an example of a company that reflected that?
sentences.zh: 体现这一点的公司有什么例子？

sentences.en: You could even go back to the early 1900s and look at Henry Ford and the Ford Company and his decision to raise the average pay from $2.25 to $5.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以回到20世纪初，看看亨利·福特和福特公司，以及他决定将平均工资从2.25美元提高到5美元的决定。

sentences.en: Back in 1914, Ford had revolutionized assembly line production.
sentences.zh: 早在1914年，福特就彻底革新了流水线生产。

sentences.en: And to keep his workers from quitting, he announced he would raise their pay to a generous $5 a day, twice what they earned before
sentences.zh: 为了防止工人离职，他宣布将他们的工资提高到慷慨的每天5美元，是他们以前的两倍，

sentences.en: and twice what they could earn at any other auto company.
sentences.zh: 也是他们在任何其他汽车公司所能赚到的两倍。

sentences.en: He believed that it was important for his employees not only to have a fair wage,
sentences.zh: 他认为，对他的员工来说，不仅要有一份公平的工资很重要，

sentences.en: but to have a wage that might give them an opportunity to actually buy the car that he was selling.
sentences.zh: 而且还要有一份能让他们有机会真正买得起他所销售的汽车的工资。

sentences.en: It was a simple American bargain.
sentences.zh: 这是一项简单的美国契约。

sentences.en: Security and high wages in exchange for hard work.
sentences.zh: 以辛勤工作换取安全感和高工资。

sentences.en: And then you can look even at so many companies, whether they be IBM, General Electric,
sentences.zh: 然后你甚至可以看看这么多的公司，无论是IBM、通用电气，

sentences.en: so many big American companies between 1930 and 1970 that created defined pension programs for their
sentences.zh: 在1930年到1970年间，许多美国大公司为他们的员工创建了确定的养老金计划，

sentences.en: employees that gave huge amounts of corporate charity to their communities that became connected in a way that made the companies intertwined with the community that they lived in.
sentences.zh: 向他们的社区捐赠了大量的企业慈善资金，以一种使企业与他们生活的社区交织在一起的方式联系起来。

sentences.en: And what exactly is the motivation for these companies to conduct themselves in this way?
sentences.zh: 这些公司以这种方式行事的动机究竟是什么？

sentences.en: As kind of community-minded corporations investing in their employees and in their communities?
sentences.zh: 作为一种具有社区意识的企业，投资于他们的员工和社区？

sentences.en: It was ultimately good for business.
sentences.zh: 这归根结底对业务有利。

sentences.en: It was the idea that if you could attract great employees and you could keep those employees,
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，如果你能吸引优秀的员工并且能够留住这些员工，

sentences.en: often for life, that you would have a better product, that you would have a better company, and that they were all inextricably tied.
sentences.zh: 通常是一辈子，你就会有更好的产品，你就会有更好的公司，它们都是密不可分的。

sentences.en: The backdrop of all of this is a post-World War II world in which the United States, in truth, is a monopoly power.
sentences.zh: 这一切的背景是二战后的世界，事实上，美国是一个垄断大国。

sentences.en: Factories were churning out products to satisfy the growing consumer appetite in America and to meet the needs of a post-war Europe.
sentences.zh: 工厂源源不断地生产产品，以满足美国日益增长的消费者需求，并满足战后欧洲的需求。

sentences.en: The defense industry kept military supplies flowing in reaction to the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 国防工业保持军用物资的流动，以应对冷战。

sentences.en: And the nation was building straight up in the cities and far out into the country.
sentences.zh: 这个国家在城市里笔直向上建造，并延伸到乡间远处。

sentences.en: America's economy was the biggest in the world.
sentences.zh: 美国的经济是世界上最大的。

sentences.en: There really is no international competition.
sentences.zh: 真的没有什么国际竞争。

sentences.en: We are it.
sentences.zh: 我们就是全部。

sentences.en: And that meant that there was a limited workforce.
sentences.zh: 这意味着劳动力是有限的。

sentences.en: And that meant that you had to be good to your people.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着你必须对你的人好。

sentences.en: Because they could go shop around for a different job.
sentences.zh: 因为他们可以去寻找别的工作。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Among the world of academics, this period was really defined as managerialism.
sentences.zh: 在学术界，这一时期确实被定义为主义管理（managerialism）。

sentences.en: The idea that you were managing the company for the people that were in it.
sentences.zh: 为了身处其中的人们而管理公司的理念。

sentences.en: And when does that start to change?
sentences.zh: 这从什么时候开始改变？

sentences.en: In the 1970s, the idea of managerialism went from being a good thing to being a very bad thing.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代，经理人主义的理念从一件好事变成了一件非常坏的事。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because investors, the shareholders, started to raise their hand and say, ah, over here, we're actually the people who own you.
sentences.zh: 因为投资者，即股东，开始举手说，啊，这边，我们实际上才是拥有你们的人。

sentences.en: And we think that you're mismanaging the company.
sentences.zh: 我们认为你们在管理公司方面做得很糟糕。

sentences.en: That you're spending too much money on your own people.
sentences.zh: 你们在自己人身上花太多钱了。

sentences.en: That you're fat and happy.
sentences.zh: 你们养尊处优。

sentences.en: There was a view that managerialism had been perverted and abused.
sentences.zh: 有一种观点认为，经理人主义已经被歪曲和滥用了。

sentences.en: And at the same time, you had the rise of Milton Friedman.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，米尔顿·弗Friedman（弗里德曼）崛起了。

sentences.en: First of all, tell me, is there some society you know that doesn't run on greed?
sentences.zh: 首先，告诉我，你知道有什么社会不是靠贪婪运转的吗？

sentences.en: You think Russia doesn't run on greed?
sentences.zh: 你以为俄罗斯不是靠贪婪运转的吗？

sentences.en: You think China doesn't run on greed?
sentences.zh: 你以为中国不是靠贪婪运转的吗？

sentences.en: What is greed?
sentences.zh: 什么是贪婪？

sentences.en: Of course, none of us are greedy.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们当中没有人是贪婪的。

sentences.en: It's only the other fellow who's greedy.
sentences.zh: 只有别人才是贪婪的。

sentences.en: The world runs on individuals pursuing their separate interests.
sentences.zh: 世界是由追求各自利益的个人运转的。

sentences.en: He's an economist at the University of Chicago who really becomes one of the most popular figures of this time.
sentences.zh: 他是芝加哥大学的一位经济学家，确实成为了这个时代最受欢迎的人物之一。

sentences.en: Not just in the world of corporate America, but throughout the country.
sentences.zh: 不仅在企业美国的世界里，而且在整个国家。

sentences.en: And it's in large part because he has a provocative view about the way we do business.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为他对我们经商方式有着挑衅性的观点。

sentences.en: And he pens this famous piece, actually in the New York Times Magazine, with the headline,
sentences.zh: 他实际上在《纽约时报杂志》上撰写了这篇著名的文章，标题是，

sentences.en: The Social Responsibility of Business is to Increase Its Profits.
sentences.zh: 企业的社会责任是增加其利润。

sentences.en: Let me read you what he wrote.
sentences.zh: 让我读读他写的内容。

sentences.en: He wrote, And what does it mean to say that business has responsibilities?
sentences.zh: 他写道：“说企业有责任是什么意思？”

sentences.en: He almost asked it rhetorically.
sentences.zh: 他几乎是在自问自答。

sentences.en: And then he writes,
sentences.zh: 然后他写道：

sentences.en: Businessmen who talk this way are unwitting puppets of the intellectual forces that have been undermining the basis of a free society these past decades.
sentences.zh: “这样说话的商人们，是过去几十年一直在破坏自由社会基础的思想力量的不自觉傀儡。”

sentences.en: It's effectively a rebuke of the way business has been managed.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是对企业管理方式的斥责。

sentences.en: It's a rebuke of managerialism.
sentences.zh: 这是对经理人主义的斥责。

sentences.en: And what does Friedman believe will happen if corporations don't see social responsibility as part of their job?
sentences.zh: 如果企业不将社会责任视为其工作的一部分，弗里德曼认为会发生什么？

sentences.en: If they just focus on what he says they should, which is profits and shareholders?
sentences.zh: 如果他们只关注他所说的他们应该关注的，即利润和股东？

sentences.en: He fundamentally believes that if you focus on profits, everything else will come with.
sentences.zh: 他从根本上认为，如果你专注于利润，其他一切都会随之而来。

sentences.en: That a company that is not as profitable as it humanly can be will ultimately lose out to other companies that are.
sentences.zh: 一家利润达不到人力极限的公司，最终会在竞争中输给那些达到的公司。

sentences.en: And you need a strong company to employ people who will pay taxes to the community, who will give charitable giving to others down the line.
sentences.zh: 你需要一家强大的公司来雇用员工，他们向社区纳税，并向其他人进行慈善捐赠。

sentences.en: So all those functions of the traditional corporation that came before, they get served through a healthy company that profitably serves its shareholders.
sentences.zh: 因此，传统企业之前的所有这些功能，都是通过一家健康地为股东服务盈利的公司来实现的。

sentences.en: I don't think they called a trickle down then, but they would now.
sentences.zh: 我想他们当时不叫涓滴经济学，但现在会了。

sentences.en: What are you going to do for the people who are out of work when the public at large decides it's not going to go in big cars, it's going to go in little cars?
sentences.zh: 当广大公众决定不再买大车而要买小车时，你将为失业的人做些什么？

sentences.en: I don't want to do a thing.
sentences.zh: 我什么也不想做。

sentences.en: I want to let the private market work.
sentences.zh: 我想让私人市场发挥作用。

sentences.en: The private market system is a system of profit and loss.
sentences.zh: 私人市场体系是一个盈亏体系。

sentences.en: And the loss part is just as essential as the profit part.
sentences.zh: 而亏损的部分和盈利的部分一样重要。

sentences.en: It is a disgrace.
sentences.zh: 这简直是耻辱。

sentences.en: He was a free marketeer.
sentences.zh: 他是一个自由市场主义者。

sentences.en: This was all part of a larger free market theory that profits above everything else would ultimately win the day and make the country stronger.
sentences.zh: 这都是更大自由市场理论的一部分，即高于一切的利润最终会胜利，并使国家变得更强大。

sentences.en: So you have this confluence of these two ideas, Milton Friedman on one side, and shareholders that are starting to look at companies and saying,
sentences.zh: 所以你拥有这两种思想的交汇，一方面是米尔顿·弗里德曼，另一方面是开始审视公司的股东，并说，

sentences.en: maybe they're a little too fat and happy.
sentences.zh: 也许他们有点太养尊处优了。

sentences.en: And that really brings about a new era in corporate America where the shareholder becomes the top priority.
sentences.zh: 这确实带来了美国企业界的新时代，股东成为首要任务。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 立即下载Times应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Andrew, once the idea of the shareholder takes hold in the U.S., how does that actually play out?
sentences.zh: 安德鲁，一旦股东的理念在美国扎根，这实际上是如何发挥作用的？

sentences.en: How does corporate behavior change?
sentences.zh: 企业行为是如何改变的？

sentences.en: It manifests itself first in the form of what became known as corporate raiders.
sentences.zh: 它首先以被称为企业突袭者的形式表现出来。

sentences.en: Investors who basically started knocking on the door of companies saying, you need to make more profits, and if you don't, we're going to take you over.
sentences.zh: 投资者基本上开始敲响公司的大门，说，你们需要赚更多的利润，如果不这样，我们将接管你们。

sentences.en: And what period is this, roughly?
sentences.zh: 这大约是什么时期？

sentences.en: This is the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 这是20世纪80年代。

sentences.en: It takes a certain breed of stock market investor, the kind with lots of money and lots of guts, to thrive in queasy times like these.
sentences.zh: 要在这样令人不安的时代蓬勃发展，需要某种特定品种的股市投资者，那种拥有大量资金和巨大勇气的投资者。

sentences.en: This is greed is good.
sentences.zh: 这就是“贪婪是美好的”。

sentences.en: This is the midst of this sort of rush around Wall Street, around capitalism.
sentences.zh: 这是华尔街周围、资本主义周围这种狂热的中期。

sentences.en: Carl Icahn is one of that breed.
sentences.zh: 卡尔·伊坎就是这种人中的一员。

sentences.en: He has a knack for turning someone else's loss into profit for himself.
sentences.zh: 他有一种将别人的损失转化为自己利润的诀窍。

sentences.en: And you had some very early investors like Carl Icahn.
sentences.zh: 你有一些像卡尔·伊坎这样的早期投资者。

sentences.en: I was always good at making money.
sentences.zh: 我一直很擅长赚钱。

sentences.en: I always was good.
sentences.zh: 我一直都很擅长。

sentences.en: Go to some of the biggest companies in the world, the TWAs of the world, one of the biggest airlines in the country.
sentences.zh: 去世界上一些最大的公司，像环球航空公司这样的公司，该国最大的航空公司之一。

sentences.en: Go to companies like U.S.
sentences.zh: 去像美国

sentences.en: Steel and say, I'm going to buy you.
sentences.zh: 钢铁这样的公司说，我要买下你。

sentences.en: Got some breaking news for you.
sentences.zh: 为你带来一些突发新闻。

sentences.en: This time, Carl Icahn is at it again.
sentences.zh: 这一次，卡尔·伊坎又来了。

sentences.en: He has offered to buy commercial metals for $15 a share.
sentences.zh: 他提出以每股15美元的价格收购商业金属公司。

sentences.en: He already owns about 10%.
sentences.zh: 他已经拥有大约10%的股份。

sentences.en: I'm going to take you over.
sentences.zh: 我要接管你。

sentences.en: I'm going to throw your CEO out.
sentences.zh: 我要解雇你的CEO。

sentences.en: I'm going to lay off scores of employees.
sentences.zh: 我要裁掉大批员工。

sentences.en: I'm going to undo all the benefit prograMs.
sentences.zh: 我要取消所有的福利计划。

sentences.en: And I'm going to manage this company in a much leaner way.
sentences.zh: 我要以一种精简得多方式来管理这家公司。

sentences.en: That was the euphemism, leaner.
sentences.zh: 这就是委婉的说法，精简。

sentences.en: Because leaner was, in their minds, stronger.
sentences.zh: 因为在他们看来，精简就是强大。

sentences.en: Leaner was more profitable.
sentences.zh: 精简意味着更有利可图。

sentences.en: So these corporate raiders were emboldened by this new guiding philosophy that it was good and right to cut the fat, cut the excess, and increase profits.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些企业突袭者受到这种新指导哲学的鼓舞，认为削减臃肿、削减多余和增加利润是美好且正确的。

sentences.en: And that that was actually the socially responsible thing to do, no matter how ruthless it might have seemed.
sentences.zh: 而且这实际上是在社会上负责任的做法，无论它看起来多么冷酷无情。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And Milton Friedman had almost turned it into a moral argument so that these investors had a moral underpinning for what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 米尔顿·弗里德曼几乎将其变成了一个道德论点，以便这些投资者为他们的所作所为找到了道德基础。

sentences.en: And how does that era of corporate raids affect the larger American business world?
sentences.zh: 那个时代的企业并购是如何影响更大的美国商业世界的？

sentences.en: These CEOs start to really internalize what they're seeing in the headlines with these corporate raiders.
sentences.zh: 这些首席执行官开始真正内化他们在头条新闻中看到的这些企业突袭者的行为。

sentences.en: They don't want to be the next target of these guys.
sentences.zh: 他们可不想成为这些家伙的下一个目标。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, CEOs that historically might have been a little bit looser with the purse say to themselves, you know what?
sentences.zh: 突然之间，那些以往对钱包可能稍微有点松懈的首席执行官心里想，你知道吗？

sentences.en: We should maybe cut back on some of these employees.
sentences.zh: 我们也许应该裁减其中一些员工。

sentences.en: We don't need all of these people.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要这么多人。

sentences.en: We need higher profits.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更高的利润。

sentences.en: Maybe instead of investing in research and development, we should start buying back our stock or dividending out money to our shareholders.
sentences.zh: 也许与其投资于研发，我们不如开始回购股票或向股东派发股息。

sentences.en: Maybe we should rethink our defined pension contributions and move towards 401k plans, which will cost us less.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该重新考虑我们的固定养老金缴款，转向成本更低的401k计划。

sentences.en: Maybe that charitable budget that we had for the community, maybe we should scale that back.
sentences.zh: 也许我们为社区设立的慈善预算，也许我们应该缩减它。

sentences.en: Over the next 20 and 30 years, you saw a massive restructuring of corporate America that put the shareholder first, the shareholder over the stakeholder.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20到30年里，你看到了美国企业的大规模重组，将股东放在首位，将股东置于利益相关者之上。

sentences.en: You saw scores of layoffs.
sentences.zh: 你看到了大量的裁员。

sentences.en: Millions of people were laid off over this period.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，数百万的人被解雇。

sentences.en: You saw charitable contributions by companies fall in half during this period.
sentences.zh: 你看到公司在此期间的慈善捐款减少了一半。

sentences.en: You saw pension funds and retirement funds diminish materially.
sentences.zh: 你看到养老金和退休金大幅缩水。

sentences.en: All of this leads to a mindset in the corner office among the CEO world of being very short-term oriented.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切导致首席执行官世界里的大佬们形成了一种极度短视的心态。

sentences.en: They all want to hit their quarterly numbers.
sentences.zh: 他们都想达成季度业绩目标。

sentences.en: Their bonuses become tied to the quarterly numbers.
sentences.zh: 他们的奖金与季度业绩挂钩。

sentences.en: Everything is now around the stock price.
sentences.zh: 现在一切都围绕着股价。

sentences.en: How high is the stock price?
sentences.zh: 股价有多高？

sentences.en: Everybody's getting compensated in stock.
sentences.zh: 每个人的薪酬都是用股票支付的。

sentences.en: And in some ways, that's supposed to incentivize managers to do the right thing, to align their interests with the shareholders.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这本该是为了激励管理者做正确的事，将他们的利益与股东保持一致。

sentences.en: But at the same time, it often pitted them against their own colleagues.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，它往往让他们与自己的同事对立起来。

sentences.en: Andrew, is there a sense that this Miltonian shareholder first system, that it works in this period?
sentences.zh: 安德鲁，是否有一种感觉，这种米尔顿式的股东至上系统，在这个时期是行之有效的？

sentences.en: You know, some people loved Milton Friedman.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些人喜欢米尔顿·弗里德曼。

sentences.en: Some people thought he was absolutely wrong.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为他大错特错。

sentences.en: But within the world of corporate America, it became a mantra.
sentences.zh: 但在美国企业界内部，它成了一种口头禅。

sentences.en: This had permeated the brains of the CEO community so much so that by 1997, the Business Roundtable actually changed their mission statement then and said, quote,
sentences.zh: 这种思想已经如此深入首席执行官群体的大脑，以至于到1997年，商业圆桌会议实际上修改了他们的使命宣言，并表示，原话是

sentences.en: the paramount duty of management and of boards of directors is to the corporation's stockholders.
sentences.zh: 管理层和董事会的首要责任是对公司的股东负责。

sentences.en: So, Andrew, how do we get to this week, this statement from this group of America's most powerful CEOs,
sentences.zh: 那么，安德鲁，我们是如何走到这一周的，面对美国最具权势的首席执行官群体发表的这份声明，

sentences.en: rejecting this philosophy that you've just described as basically accepted wisdom in American business, that shareholders should be first?
sentences.zh: 拒绝了你刚才描述的、被美国商界基本上视为公认智慧的哲学，即股东应该至上？

sentences.en: Why would they suddenly reject that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么会突然拒绝这一点？

sentences.en: I'd point back 10 years ago to the financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 我要把时间拨回10年前的金融危机。

sentences.en: For Wall Street, it was another case of whiplash.
sentences.zh: 对华尔街来说，这是又一次沉重的打击。

sentences.en: The markets haven't been this volatile in almost 80 years.
sentences.zh: 近80年来，市场从未如此动荡过。

sentences.en: To a moment where so much of this crystallized in a national conversation.
sentences.zh: 在一个将这一切大量凝聚成国家对话的时刻。

sentences.en: The market is not functioning properly.
sentences.zh: 市场没有正常运作。

sentences.en: There has been a widespread loss of confidence.
sentences.zh: 人们对信心的丧失已经十分普遍。

sentences.en: Around the role of businesses, around the role of banks, which had taken on these short-term interests at the expense of the entire country,
sentences.zh: 围绕着企业的角色，围绕着银行的角色，这些银行为了全中国的利益牺牲了自己，承担了这些短期利益，

sentences.en: where questions about capitalism were raised.
sentences.zh: 有关资本主义的问题被提了出来。

sentences.en: All across the country, plants are closing and employees are being laid off.
sentences.zh: 在全国各地，工厂在关闭，员工在被裁员。

sentences.en: For every job opening, there are six people looking to fill it.
sentences.zh: 每一个工作岗位空缺背后，都有六个人在寻找工作。

sentences.en: And when we were living at a time of unemployment of 10 percent, it really changed the narrative about what a company does.
sentences.zh: 当我们生活在10%失业率的时代时，它确实改变了关于公司做什么的叙事。

sentences.en: And people felt it.
sentences.zh: 人们切身感受到了这一点。

sentences.en: They felt it in their bones because there were so many layoffs.
sentences.zh: 他们刻骨铭心地感受到了，因为有那么多的裁员。

sentences.en: And it became a political story.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一个政治故事。

sentences.en: The ascendancy of Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·沃伦的崛起。

sentences.en: People feel like the system is rigged against them.
sentences.zh: 人们觉得这个系统对他们不公。

sentences.en: And here's the painful part.
sentences.zh: 痛苦的部分来了。

sentences.en: They're right.
sentences.zh: 他们是对的。

sentences.en: The ascendancy of Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯的崛起。

sentences.en: Yeah, corporate greed is running this country.
sentences.zh: 是的，企业贪婪正在统治这个国家。

sentences.en: And corporate greed is destroying the dreams and aspirations of millions of American people.
sentences.zh: 企业贪婪正在摧毁数百万美国人民的梦想和愿望。

sentences.en: And so much of the country started to ask real questions.
sentences.zh: 全国上下很多人开始提出真正的问题。

sentences.en: And I think that the CEO community has had a realization that if they don't change their ways, if they don't at least nod to these issues, that capitalism itself,
sentences.zh: 我认为首席执行官群体已经意识到，如果他们不改变方式，如果他们至少不对这些问题点点头，那么资本主义本身，

sentences.en: that the system itself that they've been living in will change.
sentences.zh: 他们生活其中的那个系统本身将会改变。

sentences.en: That the political forces in this country will change them for them.
sentences.zh: 这个国家的政治力量将会为他们做出改变。

sentences.en: So this evolution, this statement, is about shifting public opinion, not, again, altruism.
sentences.zh: 所以这种演变，这份声明，是关于转变公众舆论，而不是再次谈论利他主义。

sentences.en: These CEOs are reading the tea leaves.
sentences.zh: 这些首席执行官们正在察言观色。

sentences.en: They're looking at the polls and the politics.
sentences.zh: 他们在关注民意调查和政治风向。

sentences.en: And that is telling them that it's good business to change the way that they're doing business.
sentences.zh: 这告诉他们，改变经营方式是好的商业做法。

sentences.en: This is straight survival instinct.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是出于生存本能。

sentences.en: They're doing this because they think it's good for their business.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是因为他们认为这对他们的生意有利。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's talk about this statement and the people who put it out.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们来谈谈这份声明以及发表它的人。

sentences.en: I wonder what would actually change about the behavior of corporations if they put into practice what they're saying here, if they actually mean it.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，如果企业将他们在这里所说的话付诸实践，如果他们是认真的，那么他们的行为到底会发生什么变化。

sentences.en: Like how does the CEO of J.P.
sentences.zh: 比如摩根大通的首席执行官、

sentences.en: Morgan, one of the people who signed it, Jamie Dimon's job change if he puts into practice this change in approach that this document outlines,
sentences.zh: 签署人之一杰米·戴蒙，如果他将这份文件概述的这种方法的改变付诸实践，他的工作会有什么变化，

sentences.en: where shareholders are just one of a dozen people he now thinks of his corporation as serving.
sentences.zh: 在这个新方法中，股东只是他现在认为自己的公司所服务的十几个群体之一。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you my hopefully skeptical but not cynical view.
sentences.zh: 我要向你表达我希望是怀疑但并非愤世嫉俗的观点。

sentences.en: I think that there is some element of progress here because it changes the conversation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里有一些进步的成分，因为它改变了对话。

sentences.en: It provides for an allowance, if you will, for a board of directors or a CEO to say, you know what, let's raise the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，它为董事会或首席执行官提供了一种许可，可以说，你知道吗，让我们提高最低工资吧。

sentences.en: Let's actually spend the money on this plant.
sentences.zh: 让我们真正把钱花在这个工厂上。

sentences.en: Let's increase our research and development budget.
sentences.zh: 让我们增加研发预算。

sentences.en: You know what, in this community, maybe we should give a little bit more and increase our charitable giving budget.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，在这个社区里，也许我们应该多奉献一点，增加我们的慈善捐赠预算。

sentences.en: You know what, we're not going to nail our profit number next quarter because we're going to invest in these other things.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我们下个季度不去拼命达成利润数字了，因为我们要投资这些别的事情。

sentences.en: And it's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系的。

sentences.en: And that's okay.
sentences.zh: 这没关系。

sentences.en: Because before there wouldn't have been an allowance for that.
sentences.zh: 因为在此之前，根本不会有这样的许可。

sentences.en: There might not have been an allowance for that.
sentences.zh: 可能不会有这样的许可。

sentences.en: In certain boardrooms in America, there was no allowance for not hitting your profit number.
sentences.zh: 在美国某些董事会里，没有不达到利润数字的余地。

sentences.en: Now there may be.
sentences.zh: 现在也许有了。

sentences.en: That would be the positive view of this.
sentences.zh: 这将是对此事的正面看法。

sentences.en: That's not all that optimistic.
sentences.zh: 这并不是那么乐观。

sentences.en: Well, the negative view of this is that they're words on a page and that's all they are.
sentences.zh: 好吧，消极的看法是，这些只是纸面上的文字，仅此而已。

sentences.en: Politicians will look at this, maybe give them credit for it, maybe not.
sentences.zh: 政客们会看到这一点，也许会给他们点赞，也许不会。

sentences.en: And what does it cost them?
sentences.zh: 这对他们有什么代价？

sentences.en: Their signature on a piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 他们在纸上签了个名。

sentences.en: They got a front page story in the New York Times out of it.
sentences.zh: 他们因此上了《纽约时报》的头版。

sentences.en: They got a daily podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们上了一个每日播客。

sentences.en: There's safety in numbers here.
sentences.zh: 人多力量大，这里面有安全感。

sentences.en: That's probably the best that can be said about this.
sentences.zh: 这可能是对此事最好的评价了。

sentences.en: I don't hear you saying that you think this is representing a fundamental change in how corporations see themselves or function.
sentences.zh: 我没听出你认为这代表了企业对自身看法或运作方式的根本转变。

sentences.en: I still think that ultimately, if these companies are not profitable, that these executives are going to lose their jobs.
sentences.zh: 我仍然认为，归根结底，如果这些公司不盈利，这些高管就会丢掉饭碗。

sentences.en: Full stop.
sentences.zh: 句号。

sentences.en: I still think the investment community is very short-term.
sentences.zh: 我仍然认为投资界是非常短视的。

sentences.en: I think we are, over the long term, on a journey where social responsibility is going to be a central piece, at least a piece of this larger puzzle.
sentences.zh: 我认为从长远来看，我们正在踏上一段旅程，社会责任将成为核心部分，至少是这个宏大拼图中的一部分。

sentences.en: I think it's almost impossible that it's not going to be.
sentences.zh: 我认为它几乎不可能不是这样。

sentences.en: And I think you're seeing it in the voices of politicians, in the voices of the public, in the voices of regulators.
sentences.zh: 我想你在政客的声音中、在公众的声音中、在监管者的声音中都看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And as a function of that, companies are listening.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，企业正在倾听。

sentences.en: But only because social responsibility is also good for business and good for profits and good for shareholders.
sentences.zh: 但只是因为社会责任对生意有利，对利润有利，对股东也有利。

sentences.en: At the end of the day, CEOs are only going to do things that are ultimately profitable.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，首席执行官只会做那些最终能盈利的事情。

sentences.en: And in this moment, thinking about all of these other stakeholders may be profitable.
sentences.zh: 而在此时此地，考虑到所有这些其他的利益相关者可能是盈利的。

sentences.en: Ultimately, if you're looking for a big social change, I don't think you're going to look to corporate leaders for that.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，如果你在寻求重大的社会变革，我认为你不应该指望企业领袖来实现这一点。

sentences.en: I don't think that's where it's going to come from.
sentences.zh: 我认为变革不会从那里产生。

sentences.en: Companies ultimately have to be profitable entities.
sentences.zh: 公司归根结底必须是营利性实体。

sentences.en: If they're not profitable, they don't exist, and they can't serve any of these other purposes, which is, to some degree, what Milton Friedman was trying to say.
sentences.zh: 如果它们不盈利，它们就不复存在，也就无法服务于任何其他目的，这在某种程度上正是米尔顿·弗里德曼试图表达的。

sentences.en: Andrew, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: From the President of the Republic, to officially communicate the interruption of this government experience, and to raise my hand in his hands as President of the Council.
sentences.zh: 从共和国总统那里，正式传达中断这次政府经历的意愿，并在作为参议院议长的他的手中举起我的手。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, Italian Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte resigned.
sentences.zh: 周二，意大利总理朱塞佩·孔特辞职。

sentences.en: After his government, a 14-month-old coalition of populists and nationalists who are skeptical of the European Union collapsed.
sentences.zh: 此前，他的政府——一个由对欧盟持怀疑态度的民粹主义者和民族主义者组成的、仅维持了14个月的执政联盟——垮台了。

sentences.en: His resignation was triggered by one of Conte's own ministers, Matteo Salvini,
sentences.zh: 他的辞职是由孔特自己的部长马泰奥·萨尔维尼引发的，

sentences.en: an increasingly popular right-wing figure who called for a vote of no confidence in Conte's government, and who has now plunged the country into political uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 他是一个日益受欢迎的右翼人物，呼吁对孔特政府进行不信任投票，现在已经将该国陷入了政治不确定性之中。

sentences.en: Anne.
sentences.zh: 安.

sentences.en: Yes, any questions, gentlemen?
sentences.zh: 好的，还有什么问题吗，各位先生？

sentences.en: Mr. President, what sort of contingency steps or plans is the White House thinking about to stave off any kind of economic slowdown?
sentences.zh: 总统先生，白宫正在考虑采取什么样的应急步骤或计划来抵御任何形式的经济放缓？

sentences.en: What are you looking at?
sentences.zh: 你们在关注什么？

sentences.en: We're looking at various tax reductions, but I'm looking at that all the time anyway.
sentences.zh: 我们正在研究各种减税措施，不过我无论如何一直在关注这个。

sentences.en: President Trump said he's weighing a set of tax cuts to stimulate the U.S.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统表示，他正在权衡一系列减税措施，以刺激美国经济，

sentences.en: economy amid growing fears it may be entering a recession.
sentences.zh: 此前人们越来越担心美国经济可能正走向衰退。

sentences.en: Payroll tax is something that we think about, and a lot of people would like to see that, and that very much affects the workers of our country.
sentences.zh: 工资税是我们正在考虑的事情，很多人都希望看到这一点，这极大地影响了我们国家的工人。

sentences.en: Trump focused on the possibility of cutting the country's payroll taxes, the percentage of a paycheck withheld by employers to comply with tax laws,
sentences.zh: 特朗普重点关注削减该国工资税的可能性，即雇主扣留工资中用于遵守税法的百分比，

sentences.en: which would immediately put money into the hands of consumers.
sentences.zh: 这将立即把钱送到消费者手中。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the president is anxious about the possibility of a recession occurring in the middle of his presidential campaign,
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，总统对在他的总统竞选期间可能发生经济衰退的可能性感到焦虑，

sentences.en: and is eager to find ways to stave off a downturn.
sentences.zh: 并渴望找到抵御经济低迷的方法。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Babarro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是遮光睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会晕厥过去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症吗，对食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程式上或在你喜欢收听的任何地方寻找《Wirecutter秀》。
